text.p: Former Wales rugby union captain and respected journalist Clem Thomas has died suddenly in hospital in Swansea at the age of 67.
Thomas, who played for the Barbarians, Swansea, Harlequins, London Welsh and Cambridge University, made 26 appearances for Wales between 1949 and 1959, leading them on nine occasions.
He was best known for the crosskick against New Zealand in 1953 which led to Ken Jones' try and Wales' last win over the All Blacks.

He was also a member of the 1955 Lions side who toured South Africa. He missed the first test because of appendicitis but recovered in time for the third and fourth tests to assist the Lions to a 2-2 series draw.
During a varied career he also stood as a political candidate in West Wales and was a butcher, auctioneer and journalist.
Thomas was a regular commentator and journalist, primarily with The Observer and The Guardian, and only two weeks ago finished a book on British Lions tours, due for publication later this year.
